```{r}
define_XgBoost_model_specification <- function(model_parameters) {
  boost_tree(
    trees = 1000,
    tree_depth = model_parameters$tree_depth,
    min_n = model_parameters$min_n,
    loss_reduction = model_parameters$loss_reduction,
    sample_size = model_parameters$sample_size,
    mtry = model_parameters$mtry,
    learn_rate = model_parameters$learn_rate
  ) |> 
    set_engine(
      "xgboost",
      eval_metric = "logloss",
      nthread = 4
    ) |> 
    set_mode("classification")
}

define_XgBoost_Data_PreprocessingRecipe <- function(train_data) {
  
  recipe(result ~ ., data = train_data) |> 
    update_role(match_id, new_role = "ID") |> 
    step_rm(
      home_result, away_result, # target variable proxies
      home_team, away_team, # Noisy, 17 factors
      date, round) |> # Using season stage for this
    step_zv(all_predictors()) |> # Remove predictors that are constant "no predictive value"
    step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> # assigns unseen factor levels "new"
    step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors()) # dummies factor variables
  
}

model_parameters <- readRDS(here("Outputs/xgb_model_parameters.rds"))

cutoff <- floor_date(Sys.Date(), unit = "weeks", week_start = 2)

train_data <- model_data |>  filter(date < cutoff)
test_data  <- model_data |>  filter(date >= cutoff)

model_specification <- define_XgBoost_model_specification(model_parameters)
  
preprocessing_recipe <- define_XgBoost_Data_PreprocessingRecipe(train_data)

modelling_workflow <- workflow() |> 
    add_model(model_specification) |> 
    add_recipe(preprocessing_recipe)
  
  set.seed(234)
  
  model_fit <- fit(modelling_workflow, data = train_data)
  
  model_fit |> 
    predict(new_data = test_data, type = "prob")
```


```{r Data Split}
cutoff <- as.Date("2025-02-01")
cutoff <- floor_date(Sys.Date(), unit = "weeks", week_start = 2)

train_data <- model_data |>  filter(date < cutoff)
test_data  <- model_data |>  filter(date >= cutoff)

N <- nrow(train_data)
number_folds <- 10
assess <- 150
skip <- 30
initial <- -(number_folds*skip+assess-N)

folds <- rolling_origin(
  data = train_data,
  initial = initial,
  assess = assess,
  skip = skip,
  cumulative = TRUE
)

metrics <- yardstick::metric_set(mn_log_loss, roc_auc, accuracy, sens, spec)
```

```{r Model Recipes}
xgb_rec <- recipe(result ~ ., data = train_data) |> 
  update_role(match_id, new_role = "ID") |> 
  step_rm(home_result, away_result,
          home_team, away_team,
          date, round) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |> 
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())

prep(xgb_rec) |> bake(train_data)

rf_rec <- recipe(result ~ ., data = train_data) |> 
  update_role(match_id, new_role = "ID") |> 
  step_rm(home_result, away_result,
          home_team, away_team,
          date, round) |> 
  step_zv(all_predictors()) |> 
  step_novel(all_nominal_predictors()) |> 
  step_dummy(all_nominal_predictors())
```

```{r Spec}
xgb_spec <- boost_tree(
  trees = tune(),
  tree_depth = tune(), 
  min_n = tune(), 
  loss_reduction = tune(),
  sample_size = tune(), 
  mtry = tune(),
  learn_rate = tune()
) |> 
  set_engine("xgboost",
             nthread = 4,
             objective = "binary:logistic",
             eval_metric = "logloss"
             ) |> 
  set_mode("classification")

rf_spec <- rand_forest(
  trees = tune(),
  mtry = tune(),
  min_n = tune()
) |> 
  set_engine("ranger", importance = "permutation") |> 
  set_mode("classification")
```

```{r Workflow}
xgb_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(xgb_spec) |> 
  add_recipe(xgb_rec)

rf_wf <- workflow() |> 
  add_model(rf_spec) |> 
  add_recipe(rf_rec)

xgb_params <- xgb_wf |> 
  extract_parameter_set_dials() |> 
  finalize(train_data)

rf_params <- rf_wf |> 
  extract_parameter_set_dials() |> 
  update(
    mtry = mtry(c(5L, 30L)),
    trees = trees(c(500L, 1500L)),
    min_n = min_n(c(0L, 40L))
  )

xgb_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  xgb_params,
  size = 40
)

rf_grid <- grid_space_filling(
  rf_params,
  size = 30
)
```

```{r xgb Tune}
set.seed(123)

xgb_tune_res <- tune_grid(
  xgb_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = xgb_grid,
  control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE, save_pred = TRUE),
  metrics = metrics
)
```

```{r}
set.seed(123)

rf_tune_res <- tune_grid(
  rf_wf,
  resamples = folds,
  grid = rf_grid,
  control = control_grid(verbose = TRUE, save_pred = TRUE),
  metrics = metrics
)
```

```{r}
xgb_tune_res |> collect_metrics() |> 
  arrange(.metric, mean)

rf_tune_res |> collect_metrics() |> 
  arrange(.metric, mean)

xgb_tune_res |> show_best(metric = "mn_log_loss")

xgb_tune_res |> show_best(metric = "roc_auc")
```

```{r}
xgb_tune_res |> show_best(metric = "mn_log_loss") |> 
  select(xgb_mean = mean, xgb_sd = std_err) |> 
  bind_cols(
    rf_tune_res |> show_best(metric = "mn_log_loss") |> 
      select(rf_mean = mean, rf_sd = std_err)
  )
```

```{r}
xgb_tune_res |> collect_metrics() |> 
  filter(.metric == "mn_log_loss") |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = mtry:sample_size,
    values_to = "value",
    names_to = "parameter"
  ) |> 
  ggplot(aes(value, mean)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - std_err, ymax = mean + std_err), colour = "red", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x")

# Lower learn rates are better, likely very noisy data that is easy to over fit too.

rf_tune_res |> collect_metrics() |> 
  filter(.metric == "mn_log_loss") |> 
  pivot_longer(
    cols = mtry:min_n,
    values_to = "value",
    names_to = "parameter"
  ) |> 
  filter(mean < 1) |> 
  ggplot(aes(value, mean)) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = mean - std_err, ymax = mean + std_err), colour = "red", linewidth = 1.5) +
  geom_point(size = 2) +
  facet_wrap(~parameter, scales = "free_x")

# lower mtry
```

```{r}
# baseline 43
home_prop <- nrow(train_data[train_data$result == "H",])/nrow(train_data)
away_prop <- nrow(train_data[train_data$result == "A",])/nrow(train_data)

test_data |> 
  mutate(binary_result = ifelse(result == "H", 1, 0),
         logloss = -(binary_result * log(home_prop) + (1-binary_result) * log(away_prop)) ) |> 
  select(logloss) |> 
  summarise(baseline_mean = mean(logloss), baseline_sd = sd(logloss)/sqrt(n()))
```

```{r}
reliability_curve_df <- xgb_preds |> 
  mutate(result = ifelse(result == "H", 1, 0)) |> 
  rename(xgb_home_pred = .pred_H) |> 
  mutate(
    xgb_pred_bins = case_when(
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.1 ~ 0.1,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.2 & xgb_home_pred > 0.1 ~ 0.2,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.3 & xgb_home_pred > 0.2 ~ 0.3,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.4 & xgb_home_pred > 0.3 ~ 0.4,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.5 & xgb_home_pred > 0.4 ~ 0.5,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.6 & xgb_home_pred > 0.5 ~ 0.6,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.7 & xgb_home_pred > 0.6 ~ 0.7,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.8 & xgb_home_pred > 0.7 ~ 0.8,
      xgb_home_pred <= 0.9 & xgb_home_pred > 0.8 ~ 0.9,
      xgb_home_pred <= 1 & xgb_home_pred > 0.9 ~ 1,
    )
  ) |> 
  group_by(xgb_pred_bins) |> 
  mutate(xgb_home_win_prop = sum(result) / n()) |> 
  ungroup()
```

```{r}
reliability_curve_df |> 
  group_by(xgb_pred_bins) |> 
  summarise(
    home_prop = first(xgb_home_win_prop),
    count = n()
  ) |> 
  filter(count > 10) |> 
  ggplot(aes(xgb_pred_bins)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = home_prop, colour = "Proportion of Home Wins")) +
  geom_abline(slope = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1)) +
  labs(
    title = "XgBoost Model Reliability Curve (n > 10)",
    x = "Model Prediction",
    y = "Proportion of Home Wins"
  )
# Hybrid is definitely best calibrated, the large drop down at 100% bin may be attributed to a small sample size, and rare occurence
```

```{r}
    cal_logloss = -mean(result * log(home_cal_pred) + (1-result) * log(away_cal_pred) ),
    ml_logloss = -mean(result * log(.pred_H) + (1-result) * log(.pred_A))
  )
```

```{r}
stack_train_data <- xgb_cal_preds |> 
  rename(xgb_home_pred = .pred_H, xgb_away_pred = .pred_A) |> 
  bind_cols(
    rf_cal_preds |> select(rf_home_pred = .pred_H, rf_away_pred = .pred_A)
  )

stack_test_data <- xgb_preds |> 
  rename(xgb_home_pred = .pred_H, xgb_away_pred = .pred_A) |> 
  bind_cols(
    rf_preds |> select(rf_home_pred = .pred_H, rf_away_pred = .pred_A)
  )

stack_glm_fit <- glm(result ~ xgb_home_pred + rf_home_pred,
    data = stack_data,
    family = "binomial")

stack_test_preds <- predict(stack_glm_fit, newdata = stack_test_data, type = "response") |> 
  as_tibble() |> 
  rename(home_stack_pred = value) |> 
  mutate(away_stack_pred = 1 - home_stack_pred) |> 
  bind_cols(stack_test_data)

stack_test_preds |> 
  mutate(result = ifelse(result == "H", 1, 0)) |> 
  summarise(
    stack_logloss = -mean(result * log(home_stack_pred) + (1-result) * log(away_stack_pred) ),
  )
```

Bayesian:

```{r}
p_oof <- xgb_tune_res |> collect_predictions() |> 
  inner_join(xgb_best_logloss) |> 
  bind_cols(
    do.call(rbind, lapply(folds$splits,assessment))
  ) |> 
  select(.pred_class, .pred_A, .pred_H, id, result = result...5, date, match_id, home_result, away_result, home_team, away_team, )
```

```{r}
# Fitting simple Bayesian Logistic Regression model to out of fold estimates
library(brms)

p_oof$logit_p_ml <- log(p_oof$.pred_H/(1-p_oof$.pred_H))
p_oof$logit_p_ml <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(p_oof$logit_p_ml, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))

# Un-informative priors

priors_cal <- c(
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept"), # intercept
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b")   # slopes
)

fit_cal <- brm(
  result ~ 1 + logit_p_ml,
  data   = p_oof,
  family = bernoulli(),
  prior  = priors_cal,
  chains = 4, iter = 2000, cores = 4
)

priors_team <- c(
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "Intercept"), # intercept
  set_prior("normal(0, 2)", class = "b"),   # slopes
  set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd")
)

fit_team <- brm(
  result ~ 1 + logit_p_ml + (1 | home_team) + (1 | away_team),
  data   = p_oof,
  family = bernoulli(),
  prior  = priors_team,
  chains = 4, iter = 2000, cores = 4
)

# Include team partial pooling (1 | home_team) + (1 | away_team) set_prior("exponential(1)", class = "sd")
```

```{r}
first_k_res <- kfold(fit_cal, k = 10)
team_k_res <- kfold(fit_team, k = 10)

first_k_res
team_k_res

# team has a stronger elpd_kfold by roughly 60, and stronger kfoldic by roughly 120, with 33 vs 1.4 complexity.
```

```{r}
summary(fit_cal)
summary(fit_team)
summary(p_oof$logit_p_ml)
sd(p_oof$logit_p_ml)
summary(p_oof$.pred_H)
```

```{r}
set.seed(234)

final_wf <- finalize_workflow(xgb_wf, xgb_best_logloss)
final_fit <- fit(final_wf, data = train_data)
ml_preds <- predict(final_fit, new_data = test_data, type = "prob") |> 
  bind_cols(test_data) |> 
  mutate(
    result = case_when(
      result == "H" ~ 1,
      result == "A" ~ 0,
      T ~ 0
    )
  )

ml_preds$logit_p_ml <- log(ml_preds$.pred_H/(1-ml_preds$.pred_H))
ml_preds$logit_p_ml <- qlogis(pmin(pmax(ml_preds$logit_p_ml, 1e-6), 1 - 1e-6))
```

```{r}
# Logloss ml

ml_preds |> 
  summarise(
    logloss = -1/n()*sum(result*log(.pred_H) + (1-result)*log(.pred_A))
  )
```

```{r}
vip(final_fit, num_features = 20L)
# Lagged scores, and lagged possessions.
```

```{r}
ep_first <- posterior_epred(
  fit_cal,
  newdata = ml_preds,
  re_formula = NULL
)
ep_team <- posterior_epred(
  fit_team,
  newdata = ml_preds,
  re_formula = NULL
)
phat_first <- colMeans(ep_first)
phat_team <- colMeans(ep_team)

logloss_first <- -mean(
  ml_preds$result * log(phat_first) +
    (1 - ml_preds$result) * log(1 - phat_first)
)
logloss_team <- -mean(
  ml_preds$result * log(phat_team) +
    (1 - ml_preds$result) * log(1 - phat_team)
)
```

So far, Bayesian did not improve ML model.
